_note: Dose conversion factors and atmospheric dilution factors, quoted from IAEA-TECDOC-1162. This file turns a release into a dose. It contains no dose itself: a dose needs a release (layer 3), a distance, a weather class and an exposure time, all of which are runtime inputs.
_method: Inhalation and ingestion dose = intake x conversion factor, per the TECDOC's own equations (Procedure E5 step 2, Procedure E6). Ground dose = deposition x conversion factor, adjusted by the TECDOC's shielding factor and occupancy fraction (Procedure E3 step 3). Air concentration = release rate x dilution factor / wind speed (Procedure E5a). No equation here is this project's own.

_source.citation: International Atomic Energy Agency, Generic Procedures for Assessment and Response during a Radiological Emergency, IAEA-TECDOC-1162, IAEA, Vienna (August 2000)

_basisPolicy: Each factor is labelled with what it represents. 'conservative' means the source chose the highest value across body types and chemical forms, so a dose computed from it is an upper bound, not a best estimate. 'adult' means the adult value. This distinction is carried into the data because a conservative number presented as a best estimate is a lie of the same kind as a guessed number.

_dispersion.validity: constant release rate, wind direction and speed; simple terrain; ground-level release; no rain; single release point. The TECDOC states these conditions explicitly and this project does not extend the factors beyond them.
_dispersion.belowHalfKm: the TECDOC uses Fig. E1 below 0.5 km because building wake dominates; the table value at 0.5 km is used here and the limitation is recorded rather than hidden

_stabilityClasses.meaning: A most unstable, F most stable; Table E9 of the TECDOC maps weather to a class and Table E10 maps observable effects to a wind speed

_notInThisFile: No shielding factor or occupancy fraction (TECDOC Table E4: shielding 0.2-0.5 depending on building, default occupancy 0.6). No resuspension. No aquatic pathway. No internal biokinetics beyond the committed-dose factors themselves.
